Raster interrupt at line 91, where the deck view starts. After a short delay it sets the deck's background colour from $5A, the vertical and horizontal fine scroll from $49 and $48, the text mode from $6F1C (one colour, $C0, on the deck; multicolour, $D0, on the side view and the transfer board), and the blank character set at $4000 ($D018 = $21) for the band above the deck. Chains to irq_deck at line 118, and sets that handler's delay ($6F4F) to 1 when the vertical scroll $49 is 6, otherwise 7, so its writes land at the same place on the line.

irq_top's value for $D016, the operand of LDA #$D0 at $6F1B (the fine scroll is ORed in): $C0, one-colour text, for the deck, the title pages and the text pages; $D0, multicolour text, for the side view and the transfer board. Six writes: $C0 by restart, back_to_play, lift and text_page; $D0 by draw_side and transfer.

Raster interrupt at line 118. After the delay set by irq_top it switches to the character set chosen in its operand at $6F55 ($2F, the deck's tiles at $7800, during play; the game rewrites it to $2D for the text font or $21 for the blank set), sets the background from $2C, enables the sprite collision interrupt as well, and sets the next interrupt at line 246, with the screen's 25th row bit cleared. Copies the sprite shapes the game chose ($020D-$0214) into the screen's sprite pointers, clears the frame flag $4B, chains to irq_collide and calls the sound driver.
irq_deck's delay loop count, the operand of LDA #$07 at $6F4E: irq_top makes it 1 when the vertical fine scroll is 6, otherwise 7.
irq_deck's value for $D018, the operand of LDA #$2F at $6F54: $2F the deck's characters at $7800, $2D the text font at $7000, $21 the blank set at $4000.

The interrupt at line 246, below the deck, or earlier, at the moment two sprites first touch on the deck, since irq_deck enabled the collision interrupt for this stretch. Turns the sprite collision interrupt off again, sets the next interrupt at line 254 (irq_bottom), keeps the sprite-to-sprite collisions the frame produced in $4F (reading $D01E clears it), and calls cassette_motor.

The text font ($D018 = $2D), 256 characters of 8 bytes: the status line above the deck (irq_bottom) and the console's text pages (text_page). Letters and digits are two rows tall, the top half at the code and the bottom at the code plus $80; the capitals and the wide m and w are two columns wide as well, their right half at the code plus $20.
The text font's characters $80-$FF, the bottom halves of the two-row letters and digits.

The deck's character set ($D018 = $2F), shown in one colour on the deck, the title pages and the deck plan, and in multicolour on the side view and the transfer board: the tiles of the deck map's blocks, the two-row letters of the title pages, and the board's wires and pieces. This is character 0; rotate_chars' instructions name characters 0-3 until next_anim first rewrites them.
Character 1 of the deck's set, named by rotate_chars' instructions as loaded.
Character 2 of the deck's set, named by rotate_chars' instructions as loaded.
Character 3 of the deck's set, named by rotate_chars' instructions as loaded.
The deck's characters $80-$FF: the bottom halves of the title's letters, the side view's characters (the ship picture's cells plus $80) and the transfer board's $F1-$FD.

The dictionary of the droid descriptions and console pages: a count, 249, then the words, each starting with a byte with bit 7 set, in the game's alphabet. index_words lists their addresses at $4400/$4500, and a word is printed by its number: 0 "influence" to 248 "awarded".
The dictionary from inside word 160, "clamp": words 161, "lower", to 248, "awarded", whose end runs up to the effects at $C610.

The sound effects, 31 records of 16 bytes for numbers 1-31 (start_effect): an instrument from $EAA0, then the channel's frequency, pitch slide, slide period count and reload, count of periods, pulse width, pulse slide, mode, restart frequency and follow-on effect. 1-4 are the four weapons' shots, 5 the game over, 6 a new game, 7 the beam-in, 8 low energy, 9-$0E the transfer and its results, $0F the static, $10 the lift, $11 a hit, $12 an explosion, $13 the 001's end, $14 the energiser, $15 and $16 the console, $17 a deck cleared, $18 the hum, $19 the player hit, $1A a ram, $1B the countdown, $1C transfer mode, $1D-$1F the title.
Bytes 5-7 of effect $18, the alert's hum (at $C780): deck_start writes the deck's three from hum_count, hum_period and hum_length here.
Byte 6 of effect $18, the hum's slide period reload, from hum_period.
Byte 7 of effect $18, the hum's count of slide periods, from hum_length.
The number of waypoints on each deck, 0-15: 5 to 24, 239 in all.
The address of each deck's waypoint list, low bytes; the lists follow at $C840-$CB0C, 3 bytes a waypoint (column, row and the ways on from it), in order of row, the first the deck's start point.
The high bytes of the waypoint lists' addresses.
For build_ship, each deck's base type before the ship number is added: places 12 down to 6 get the base plus the ship number plus a random 0-3; the deck's other places get smaller types.
The waypoint lists of decks 0-15: each waypoint a map cell, column and row, and a byte with a bit for each of the eight ways a robot may go on from it.

The title screen, the screen codes of 25 rows of 40, copied whole to the screen at $4800 by title_screen with the four pages after it; its colours come from the colour table. $CFE8-$CFFF, copied with it, are not part of the picture.

The title pages, in the RAM under the I/O: print_page records, each the map address (row and column, the row's high bits $80) and characters two rows tall up to a byte with bit 7 set, printed into the deck map, which the view then scrolls across. The first page: "Hewson Consultants Ltd. presents Paradroid", the copyright, "Plug your joystick into port 2" and the controls.
The second title page, from column 42: the story of the fleet of Robo-Freighters, the radionic beam from the asteroids and the prototype Influence Device.
The third title page, from column 82: the 001 Influence Device, its lasers, and why the host must be changed before it burns out.
Text of the third title page ("channelled towards holding control"). The code names $D852 only as colour RAM, row 2 from column 2, which colour_status fills with the I/O banked in.
Text of the third title page ("of the host robot, as it attempts"); the code names $D87A only as colour RAM, row 3 from column 2 (colour_status).
Text of the third title page ("to a new robot requires the device"); the code names $D940 only as colour RAM, the play window's first row (draw_deck, draw_plan).
The fourth title page, from column 122: what the remote terminal shows, the consoles and the three-digit numbers, whose first digit is the class.
The fifth title page, from column 170: the top and worst scores of the day, then the pause keys: fire and run-stop restart, clr-home quits, f7 cheese and f8 pause.
The top score's line, which score_line rewrites from its third byte ($DD93): "6809 - AEB" until it is beaten.
The worst score's line, rewritten from $DDBE: "6502 - TSO" until a lower score takes its place.
The credits, at the foot of the fifth page: "Paradroid programmed by Andrew Braybrook. Sound advice by Steve Turner." The record at $DEDA, with no characters, ends the pages.
Entry to the transfer board in this block, a jump to $E016. Called from $22C3.
Entry to the score check at the end of a game, a jump to $E4E5. Called from game_over.

Draws and deals the transfer board, then lets the player choose a side. The board is drawn on a red background from the rows at $E613 (three), $E68B (twelve times) and $E6B3: a bar at column 3 and one at column 36, twelve wires from each running in to the middle column at 19-20, the pulsers' columns 1 and 38. Colour RAM gives the left side yellow ($FF in $7F) and the right purple ($FC in $87), both multicolour, with the middle column's cells alternating. Then each of the twelve rows gets a piece dealt at two places on each side, columns 10 and 14 on the left and 29 and 25 on the right (place_piece), the side variables swapped between sides (swap_sides). Sprite 7, the player, and the target's sprite (slot $6B) are put at either end of row 10, each showing its own numbered shape ($48 plus its sprite), with the two hosts' classes in $88 and $83. For up to 99 steps of the delay the stick moves the player to the left (yellow) or the right (purple), $7E holding the choice, with "Colour?" and the steps left, $8A in BCD, on the status bar; fire ends the choice early. $8A is left at $99 for the transfer itself.

Deals a piece onto the wire at row ($1C), column y. On a wire cell (below $F3) a random number from the noise of voice 3, 0-15, picks from the table at $E607 by rewriting the JMP at $E243: 0 an auto-pulser, 1 a terminator, 2 a colour changer, 3 a splitter, 4 a joiner, each 1 in 16, and plain wire, 11 in 16. On an empty cell, left by a piece in the row above, a splitter is dealt 1 time in 16 when three rows are left, and otherwise the wire on its inner side is cleared (cut_inner). A cell already holding a piece ($F3 and above) is left alone.
place_piece's jump to the piece dealt, the low byte of the JMP operand at $E243, from the table at $E607.
High byte of place_piece's jump to the piece, from $E608.
Piece 0: the side's pulser character, $82, on the wire in the side's colour, so the wire is fed without a pulser being spent on it.

Piece 1: the side's end character, $7D, on the wire in the side's colour, and the wire on its inner side cleared (cut_inner), so a pulse stops there. Not dealt at the outer place of a row (column 10 or 29).
Piece 2: the square $F4 in the other side's colour, so a pulse through it arrives as the opponent's. Not dealt at the outer place of a row.

Piece 3, when at least three rows are left: if the next cell in is wire and no bar is in the way, a bar three rows tall ($F5, $F6, $F7, draw_bar) whose middle row keeps its wire from the side and whose top and bottom rows keep their wires to the middle, so one pulse reaches two segments. The top and bottom rows lose their wires from the side (cut_outer), the middle row its wire to the middle (cut_inner).

Piece 4, when at least three rows are left: a bar three rows tall like the splitter's, the other way round: the top and bottom rows keep their wires from the side and the middle row its wire to the middle, so two wires feed one segment.
Clears the three cells beyond column y on the middle side of row ($1C), and the fourth too if it is the side's wire, keeping $1C and Y.

Clears the three cells beyond column y on the edge side of row ($1C); the fourth, unless it is empty or part of a bar, gets the side's end character $7D in the side's colour, so the cut wire ends in a terminator. Keeps $1C and Y.
Moves $1C/$1D one cell towards the middle: adds the side's step $7A/$7B, +1 on the left, −1 on the right.
Moves $1C/$1D one cell towards the edge, subtracting the side's step $7A/$7B.
Points $1E/$1F at the colour RAM cell for the screen cell at $1C/$1D ($1D + $90).
Draws a bar three rows tall at column y of row ($1C) in the side's colour: $F5 on that row, $F6 and $F7 on the two below.

Swaps the variables of the two sides, so the same code deals the other side: wire characters $8C/$8D, pulser and end characters $82/$7D, colours $7F/$87, $81/$85, pulsers $80/$84, $8E/$86, and negates the step $7A/$7B.
Colours the top two rows of the middle column, $D9A3, in the colour in X, the side chosen, and keeps it in $8B.

Gives each side its pulsers: the player's host's class $88 plus 3, the target's class $83 plus 4, into $80 for the yellow side and $84 for the purple, by the side in $7E. Points $1C/$1D at the start of screen row A + 11 through the row address tables at $0CFB and $0D14, and $1E/$1F at its colour RAM.

At the end of a game: compares the 8-digit BCD score at $21-$24 with the top score of the day at $E70C. If higher, it takes the top score's place, "Great Score!" and "Please enter your initials -" are shown, the initials are entered (initials) and the line on the title page at $DD93 is rewritten (score_line). Otherwise, if lower than the worst score of the day at $E710, it takes that place, with "Lowest Score of the Day!" and the line at $DDBE. A score equal to either changes nothing.
Takes three initials into $E6EA-$E6EC (enter_letter). The second LDX #$00 repeats the first.

Lets the player choose initial $10: any push of the stick steps the letter back (up or left) or on (down or right) through the 27 at $E6F1, A to Z and a space, round at either end, shown at row 22, column 31 (the string at $E6E8) after each step of the delay; fire takes it, once released.
